# Task
Write tests for the requirements in `spec.json` against the API and modules in `design.json`. The code is
being written in parallel, so rely only on that contract. Constraints: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, the standard-library sqlite3 module for storage, pytest with fastapi.testclient.TestClient (needs httpx) for tests. Application code lives in the app/ package (entry point app/main.py exposing `app`); tests live in tests/. Configuration comes from environment variables; never hard-code secrets.
- Files under tests/ only. Name tests after requirement ids (e.g. test_r1_shorten_returns_code).
- Use fastapi.testclient.TestClient against app.main:app and isolate state (e.g. a temporary database).
- No network access and no sleeps.

# Inputs

## spec.json
{
  "title": "URL Shortener Service Specification",
  "problem_statement": "Design and build a secure, persistent HTTP URL shortener service that allows clients to create short links (with auto-generated codes or custom aliases), redirect to destination URLs with expiration handling, view access analytics, and enforce SSRF validation and rate limiting.",
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint POST /shorten to create shortened URLs with optional custom alias and optional expiration time.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given a valid payload `{\"url\": \"https://example.com\"}`, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 201 with a generated unique `code` and the complete `short_url`.",
        "Given a valid payload `{\"url\": \"https://example.com\", \"alias\": \"my-link\"}` where 'my-link' does not exist, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 201 with `code`: 'my-link'.",
        "Given a payload with an alias that already exists, when POST /shorten is called, then return HTTP 409 Conflict with an error message.",
        "Given a payload with `expires_at` in ISO 8601 format in the future, when POST /shorten is called, then store the link with the specified expiration timestamp."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R2",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint GET /{code} to redirect callers to the original target URL.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",

        "Given an active, non-expired code mapped to 'https://example.com', when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 302 Found (or 307) with 'Location: https://example.com'.",
        "Given a code that does not exist in the database, when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found.",
        "Given a code whose `expires_at` timestamp is earlier than current UTC time, when GET /{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R3",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint GET /analytics/{code} returning link usage metrics and lifecycle timestamps.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Given an existing code that has been redirected 3 times, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 200 with `total_clicks`: 3, `created_at` matching link creation time, and `last_visited_at` matching the timestamp of the last redirection.",
        "Given an existing code that has never been redirected, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 200 with `total_clicks`: 0 and `last_visited_at`: null.",
        "Given a non-existent code, when GET /analytics/{code} is received, then return HTTP 404 Not Found."

import sqlite3
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient


def test_r1_shorten_returns_201_and_code(client: TestClient):
    """R1: Given valid payload, POST /shorten returns HTTP 201 with generated code and short_url."""
    payload = {"url": "https://example.com"}
    response = client.post("/shorten", json=payload)

    assert response.status_code == 201
    data = response.json()
    assert "code" in data
    assert isinstance(data["code"], str)
    assert len(data["code"]) > 0
    assert "short_url" in data
    assert data["short_url"].endswith(data["code"])


def test_r1_shorten_with_custom_alias_returns_201(client: TestClient):
    """R1: Given payload with unused alias, POST /shorten returns HTTP 201 with code equal to alias."""
    payload = {"url": "https://example.com", "alias": "my-link"}
    response = client.post("/shorten", json=payload)

    assert response.status_code == 201
    data = response.json()
    assert data["code"] == "my-link"
    assert data["short_url"].endswith("my-link")


def test_r1_shorten_duplicate_alias_returns_409(client: TestClient):
    """R1: Given an alias that already exists, POST /shorten returns HTTP 409 Conflict."""
    payload = {"url": "https://example.com", "alias": "duplicate-alias"}
    res1 = client.post("/shorten", json=payload)
    assert res1.status_code == 201

    res2 = client.post("/shorten", json=payload)
    assert res2.status_code == 409
    error_data = res2.json()
    assert "detail" in error_data or "error" in error_data
